title: Gaussian Marker Reduction with a Constant Quadratic Fibre
summary: Reduces marked Gaussian moment series to base markers for a constant quadratic fibre, extends actual generation to nilpotent coefficient content, and computes the exact scalar specialization defect.
verification: Complete scoped written proof with internal source review; the 17 November review corrections clarify hypotheses, proof dependencies and versioned companion sources. Current build and artifact checks are recorded in verification.json. Independent mathematical review remains pending.
next_steps: Independent review of the universal even/odd certificates, nilpotent-content corollary and exact coefficient-ring defect.
Investigate purity-to-safety for one constant quadratic fibre over two ordinary base variables; the marker reduction alone does not settle it.
abstract:
Over every characteristic-zero field, a Gaussian phase that is quadratic
in one fibre variable with constant quadratic coefficient has every
polynomially marked moment series generated by base-variable markers,
time derivatives and polynomial time coefficients. Over a general $\mathbb Q$-algebra $R$, we
prove a coefficient-content theorem for the polynomial source and actual
marker generation for nilpotent coefficient content. Under the field
or unit-content hypotheses, degree bounds for base periods transfer to
the original markers. For the family $Y^2+bY$, we compute
the exact actual-image defect: it is a point module with coefficient
module $R/(bR+\Gamma_b(R))$, where $\Gamma_b(R)$ consists of elements
killed by a power of $b$. This gives a necessary and sufficient
generation criterion in that family and shows why generation after
every field specialization and every finite nilpotent quotient need
not descend to the original coefficient ring.
incorporates: A Specialization Obstruction in Gaussian Marker Generation
